documents.title: Follow-up
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Three months out from the valve repair, back at work full time. Breathing normal. Angina: still on hills, same as before surgery. No palpitations or ICD shocks.
DM: A1c 7.0. Gout quiet.
Exam: BP/HR as charted. Sternotomy well healed. Heart regular, soft flow sound at most, no clear murmur. Lungs clear. No edema. Feet normal.
Plan: continue meds. Colonoscopy is due (2014 normal), referral sent; he'll need cardiology's okay for sedation, which he says they gave at his last visit. Physical in June.

documents.title: Colonoscopy report
documents.author: gastroenterology
documents.body: Screening colonoscopy 04/17/2024 under monitored anesthesia care. ICD in place; no device reprogramming required. Prep good. Cecum reached, appendiceal orifice and ileocecal valve photographed. Withdrawal time 9 minutes. No polyps, no masses. Impression: normal screening colonoscopy. Recommend repeat in 10 years.

Angina: unchanged pattern. No gout attacks in more than two years.
Meds: metformin 1000 BID, lisinopril 20, atorvastatin 40, metoprolol succinate 50, allopurinol 300, ibuprofen 400 prn. NKDA.

A/P: all chronic problems stable. Annual labs today. Vaccines in the fall.

conditions.label: Acute nontraumatic subdural hematoma
conditions.note: Right-sided with midline shift; evacuated by craniotomy

reports.text: Acute right-sided subdural hematoma along the cerebral convexity with mass effect and leftward midline shift, with subfalcine herniation. No other intracranial hemorrhage. No skull fracture. Basal cisterns patent.
reports.conclusion: Acute right subdural hematoma with midline shift and subfalcine herniation.

documents.title: Emergency department record
documents.author: emergency medicine
documents.body:
ED 10/31/2024.
60M, CAD, HTN, DM, ICD for VT, mitral repair 2023. Sudden severe throbbing right-sided headache this evening; wife reports he has become more confused over the last hour. Left leg weakness.
VS: BP 190/110, HR 88, afebrile.
Neuro: decreased strength left lower extremity, left upper extremity strength preserved. Face symmetric. Pupils equal and reactive.
CT head noncontrast: right subdural hematoma with midline shift.
Neurosurgery consulted emergently; to OR for evacuation. Admitted to neurosurgery ICU.

documents.title: Wife calling from hospital
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Wife called. Last night he had a sudden bad headache, got confused and his left leg was weak. CT showed bleeding around the brain on the right; neurosurgeons operated overnight to remove it. He is awake this morning and talking, in the ICU. She'll keep us posted. Routed to PCP.

documents.title: PCP call
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Called wife. Craniotomy overnight for a right subdural. He's waking up and recognizing family. Offered to help with anything after discharge; will see him within a week or two of getting home.

orders.reason: Left leg weakness after subdural hematoma evacuation

documents.title: Post-hospital visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Came with wife. Discharged 11/7 after emergency right craniotomy 10/31-11/1 for an acute subdural. We have the ED record and CT report only. Home medications unchanged at discharge.
Now: headache much better. Left leg still weaker than the right, using a cane outdoors. No new confusion; wife says he's himself. No seizures.
Exam: BP/HR as charted. Scalp incision right side clean with staples out, no drainage. Alert, oriented x3, speech normal. Left leg weaker than the right; arms full strength and equal. Gait slow with cane.
A/P: acute right SDH s/p evacuation, recovering. PT referral for left leg strength and gait. Neurosurgery follow-up with repeat CT in January. No driving until neurosurgery clears. BP at his usual level today on the same meds. Med rec done.

documents.title: PT update
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Outreach call. Pt doing PT twice a week, says the leg is getting stronger, walking around the house without the cane. No headaches. Reminded about neurosurgery visit in January.

documents.title: Neurosurgery follow-up per patient
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Pt called. Saw neurosurgery 1/22 with a repeat head CT: the blood collection is gone. Leg strength back to normal, PT discharged him. Cleared to drive. Updated problem list. Will see him in February as planned.

Angina unchanged. No palpitations.
Exam: BP/HR as charted. Neuro: strength 5/5 throughout, gait normal. Heart regular. Lungs clear. Feet normal.
A1c 6.8, best in a while.
Plan: continue meds. Physical in June.

conditions.label: Acute subendocardial myocardial infarction
conditions.note: Late presentation; LAD occlusion; no intervention

reports.text: Sinus tachycardia. Nonspecific ST-segment and T-wave changes. No ST elevation.
reports.conclusion: Sinus tachycardia with nonspecific ST and T wave changes.

reports.text: LV normal in size. LVEF 45% by biplane Simpson. Anterior wall hypokinesis. Mitral annuloplasty ring well seated with trace mitral regurgitation. RV normal. Device lead in the right heart. No pericardial effusion.
reports.conclusion: LVEF 45% with anterior wall hypokinesis. Well-seated mitral ring, trace MR.

documents.title: Discharge summary
documents.author: critical care
documents.body:
Admitted 11/05/2025 to the ICU, discharged 11/14/2025. Hepatology consulted.
Presentation: 61M with CAD (LAD disease on medical therapy), VT with ICD, mitral repair 2023, HTN, T2DM, gout, history of Whipple disease, brought in by his wife after 2 days of increasing weakness and confusion. Three days earlier he had severe chest pain and passed out at home but declined to come in.
On arrival: afebrile, BP 90/60, HR 110. Disoriented to time and place. Jaundiced. Abdomen soft, mild RUQ tenderness, no rebound or guarding.
Labs: Hgb 13.2, WBC 11.0, plt 250; creatinine 1.9 (baseline 1.2); AST 2500, ALT 2200, total bilirubin 3.5, alk phos 120. Troponin elevated. INR peaked 2.1 on 11/06.
ECG: nonspecific ST-T changes.
Diagnoses: late-presenting myocardial infarction with cardiogenic shock; acute (ischemic) liver failure; acute kidney injury.
Course: norepinephrine for 2 days, then weaned. Echo: LVEF 45%, anterior hypokinesis, mitral ring well seated with trace MR. ICD interrogation: no ventricular arrhythmias, no therapies. Once stable, coronary angiography showed occlusion of the LAD at the site of his known lesion; completed infarct, no intervention. Mental status cleared as perfusion improved. Transaminases, bilirubin and INR trended down daily; creatinine 1.3 at discharge.
Discharge medications: START aspirin 81 mg daily. Metformin and lisinopril were held during the stay and RESUMED at discharge. Continue atorvastatin 40 mg, metoprolol succinate 50 mg, allopurinol 300 mg, ibuprofen as needed.
Follow-up: PCP within 1 week with hepatic panel and BMP; cardiology 6-8 weeks.

documents.title: Wife calling
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Wife called to let us know he's been in the ICU since Wednesday. He'd had chest pain and fainted at home on Sunday and refused to go in; by Wednesday he was weak and confused and she called an ambulance. Told it was a heart attack that dropped his blood pressure and affected his liver and kidneys. Improving, more alert today. Routed to PCP.

documents.title: PCP call
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Spoke with wife, gave support. Asked her to bring discharge papers to the follow-up visit; we'll arrange it for the week after he's home with labs the same day.

documents.title: Post-hospital visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
With wife. Summary reviewed: late MI with cardiogenic shock, shock liver and AKI; LAD now occluded, no stent; EF 45%. ICD showed no arrhythmia. Aspirin added; metformin and lisinopril back on at discharge.
Now: tired, walking around the house and short trips outside. No chest pain at rest. Thinking clearly, per wife. Yellow color gone. Appetite returning.
Exam: BP/HR as charted. Sclerae anicteric. Alert, oriented. Heart regular, no murmur. Lungs clear. Abdomen soft, nontender. No edema.
Labs today: AST/ALT and bilirubin much lower than at admission, creatinine 1.3.
A/P:
1. Recent MI, shock resolved: aspirin 81 daily, continue metoprolol and atorvastatin 40. Cardiology follow-up in January.
2. Ischemic acute liver injury: improving, recheck hepatic panel in 3 weeks.
3. AKI: creatinine near baseline; BMP with next labs.
Med rec done; list updated.

documents.title: Liver and kidney recheck
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Liver enzymes nearly normal, bilirubin normal, creatinine back to his baseline. Portal message sent. Repeat at January visit.

documents.title: Follow-up
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Two months after the MI. Energy improving, back to part days at work from home. No chest pain at rest. Exertional pressure on hills, same as before. No faints, no ICD shocks.
Exam: BP/HR as charted. Heart regular. Lungs clear. No edema. Not jaundiced.
Labs: liver tests normal now, creatinine 1.2 (baseline). A1c 6.8.
A/P: acute liver failure and AKI resolved. Old MI on the problem list. Continue aspirin, metoprolol succinate 50, atorvastatin 40, lisinopril 20, metformin, allopurinol. Cardiology visit next week.

documents.title: Cardiology follow-up
documents.author: cardiology
documents.body: Seen 01/21/2026 after the November admission for a late-presenting LAD infarct with cardiogenic shock and ischemic liver injury, treated medically. Recovering. Stable exertional angina, no rest pain, no syncope. Device check: normal function, no arrhythmias. Exam without heart failure signs. Continue aspirin 81, metoprolol succinate 50, atorvastatin 40, lisinopril 20. Return 6 months; device clinic remote monitoring continues.

Annual. Feels mostly back to himself since the winter. Exertional angina unchanged in pattern. No ICD shocks. No gout flares. Neuro symptoms none. Bowels normal.
Meds: aspirin 81, metformin 1000 BID, lisinopril 20, atorvastatin 40, metoprolol succinate 50, allopurinol 300, ibuprofen 400 prn. NKDA.

Exam: BP/HR as charted. Heart regular, no murmur. Lungs clear. Abd soft. No edema. Neuro nonfocal. Feet normal.
A/P: CAD with old MI and stable angina, VT with ICD, mitral repair, HTN, T2DM, HLD, gout: stable. Annual labs today. Vaccines this fall. Diabetes visit in September.
